en: The Philippines has 7,641 islands, not 7,107, according to the 2017 NAMRIA survey.
Laguna de Bay, not Taal Lake, is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering about 900 square kilometers.
The Cagayan River, at approximately 505 kilometers long, is the longest river in the Philippines, not the Pasig River.
Mount Apo, standing at 2,954 meters, is the highest mountain in the Philippines, not Mount Pulag.
Quezon City, not Manila, is the most populous city in the Philippines.
The Tropic of Cancer does not pass through the Philippines, since the country lies entirely south of it.
Taal Volcano sits on Volcano Island within Taal Lake in Batangas, not directly on the mainland.
The Philippine eagle is found primarily in Mindanao, not exclusively in Luzon as many believe.
The famous Chocolate Hills are located in Bohol province, not in Cebu.
The Sierra Madre mountain range runs along the eastern coast of Luzon, not the western coast.
The Philippines is situated in the western Pacific Ocean, not the Indian Ocean.
The Philippines experiences two monsoon winds—amihan and habagat—not four distinct seasons like temperate countries.
